scope: Measure bounded direct-read storage behavior on B550 while the Qwen3.8-Flash-Next transfer continued. Compare the 21.8-TB rotational /mnt/weights device with a same-sized NVMe scratch file, including one Strata-sized 1,382,400-byte expert-slot random-read pattern. This is a storage baseline, not a Strata model run or token-throughput measurement.

platform.scheduling: ionice class 2 priority 7, under the active downloads and GPU jobs

unused_nvme.state: not mounted; FAT32 and NTFS partitions were present
unused_nvme.action: left untouched because its identity and prior contents were not established

input.copy_note: An ordinary copy was used because GNU dd rejected direct input buffers above 512 bytes on this filesystem, while fio O_DIRECT worked. The benchmark itself used O_DIRECT.

scratch_decision.conclusion: Use an NVMe scratch staging area for runnable Qwen GGUF packs; do not stage it on /mnt/weights if expert reads miss cache.
scratch_decision.capacity: A Strata Qwen pack at roughly 33-125 GiB fits comfortably in the 2.1-TiB free root NVMe. The separate 953.9-GB NVMe also has enough capacity, but it is unmounted and contains foreign FAT/NTFS partitions, so do not format or mount it without a separate identity/data decision.
scratch_decision.staging_cost: At the measured mixed copy rate, a 70-GiB pack would take about 6 minutes to stage after download; a 125-GiB pack about 11 minutes.
scratch_decision.expected_effect: The HDD is not a large problem for sequential loading, but random expert-slot misses would add about 11.23 ms per depth-1 read versus NVMe. Even with queue depth 8, the measured HDD mean latency was 66.55 ms and NVMe was 3.64 ms.

non_claims: No Qwen model, GGUF, PLE table, or Strata pack was loaded or run.
The safetensors shard is a real Qwen file used as a storage substrate, not a runnable model artifact; its tensor layout does not emulate Strata expert placement.
These are raw fio storage measurements under active transfers and GPU jobs, not same-day model token throughput or first-token latency measurements.
A warm expert cache can hide storage latency; the expert-slot case measures cold/random misses, which is the boundary the scratch decision must survive.
The unmounted 953.9-GB NVMe was not mounted, formatted, erased, benchmarked, or otherwise changed.
No active download, GPU process, tmux session, service, or storage configuration was changed by the benchmark.
